translation:
You keep making a fuss about ghosts and
specters, but do you really believe in them?

Sure. Don't you think it's more interesting
that way?

I don't. I'd rather not have to put up with
that kind of trouble.
Well aren't you a boring guy.

If they exist, I want to see them with my own
eyes. Even a photo would do.

And if they don't, I want to know that
scientifically.
…It doesn't matter either way, right?
It absolutely does!

You only ever care enough to have a vague
understanding of things.
That's why your grades are so lackluster!
Oof… she went right for my weak point.

If you want to know something, research it
thoroughly.

If you do that, you won't have to cram
everything at the last minute.
It'll just come naturally to you.

Well that's easy to say if you're naturally
clever…

If you understand, then learn from my
example.
Well, I'll do my best in regards to my grades.
There's no such thing as gh-ghosts, right?
Huh? It's not good to assume like that.
Hyaa?!
But but, it is scientifically impossible, and…
Mikuru!
Y-yes—
That's just called narrow-mindedness.

Accept things as they truly are, without
being bound by your preconceptions.

In doing so, we can discover things that you
could never have imagined.

What I'm saying is that you need to pull
yourself together more.

Otherwise, you'll be left behind by the
ever-coming future!
R-right…
You affirm the existence of ghosts.

Well, not exactly. Wouldn't it just be
interesting if they did exist?
I've never seen one, so I want to see one.

That's why I'll always investigate any
promising leads.
So you're seeking a scientific explanation.
That's half right.

But either way, wouldn't it be more interesting
if there were ghosts and poltergeists?

Humans have to consider so many things just
by simply being alive.

So I don't think it's as simple as "Death is the
end of all things.”

Not to mention, with a little under 100 years to
live—

I don't think my curiosity will run dry that
easily!

Miss Suzumiya, do you believe in psychic
phenomena or spirits of any sort?

Sure. I think it would be interesting if they
were real.
But what about you, Koizumi?

I believe there is always a trick behind any
such phenomena.

If you dissect things scientifically, you'll
always find some reason or basis for them.
I prefer that type of conclusion.
That's just like you.

But that does kind of sound like an excuse
for being scared.
Indeed. That may be the case.

It's possible that deep within, I'm afraid of
phenomena that can't be explained.

I'd say that's a much more healthy way of
thinking than just denying it.
I'm honored to hear you say so.
